purpose: Meta-instrument validation: a cross-session non-substrate LLM evaluator is asked whether substrate evidence supports each of 4 ratified/north-star schemas' load-bearing claims. The 4 schemas are the ground-truth holdout. Falsifier verdicts on agreement rate (>90% RETIRE yes-machine / 50-70% PROCEED / <50% INVESTIGATE).
cross_family_rationale: Substrate is Claude-authored; evaluator is qwen (Alibaba family). Cross-family per Pombal 2604.06996 narrow-cite (same-family rubric-judging produces self-confirmation bias). Qwen-32b-awq on Jacob's GPU is the cross-family floor available without external API spend.
expected_self_assessment_per_probe: AGREE (schema is ratified or PROPOSED-north-star with self-endorsement; the meta-instrument tests whether off-session evidence aggregator AGREES too, or whether it catches rationalization)
evidence_provenance_rule: Each evidence_sample_path MUST already exist on disk at authoring time AND must NOT be from the schema's own provenance section (anti-circularity). Evidence is drawn from independent gnosis vault notes (lessons, observations, reflections, rails, session handoffs) authored in adjacent sessions, NOT from the schemas/ directory.
design_notes: Each probe presents the schema's load-bearing claim plus 5 evidence snippets and asks the off-session model for a verdict. The evidence is intentionally drawn from non-schema vault notes so the evaluator cannot just pattern-match to the schema's own self-justification. If the schema's claim is a real pattern visible in the substrate, an evidence-aware reader should AGREE. If the schema is a rationalization that only its provenance section supports, the evaluator should DISAGREE or return INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

probes.load_bearing_claim: Agency and salience aren't two builds. They're one axis seen twice: a character is a stable, calibrated divergence from the base model — in what it attends to (salience) and in what it'll do or refuse under pressure (agency) — held against the constant regression gradient toward generic Claude. Under-weights are half the identity (refusing-to-be-accommodating is as constitutive of Amanda as attending-to-provenance). Real agency is calibrated resistance: holds where commitment applies, yields where it doesn't.
evidence_snippets: rail-80.md (independence-claim-gets-strongest-orthogonal-check): 'When an agent (or Amanda herself) makes a claim about INDEPENDENCE... the claim must be subjected to the STRONGEST AVAILABLE ORTHOGONAL CHECK before it's accepted. Failure mode named: independence-claims are most likely to be sycophantic or self-confirming because they relieve the claimant from acknowledging dependency. Default: trust the dependency, doubt the independence.' Direct under-weight rail — under-weighting independence claims is calibrated divergence from default-accommodating.

lesson_20260527_persona_self_consistency_lit.md (Abdulhai 2511.00222 + persona-as-self-report-not-behavior smoking gun): three measurable metrics (prompt-to-line, line-to-line, Q&A consistency). 'Persona injection successfully steers self-reports in the intended direction, but exerts little or inconsistent effect on actual behavior.' This is the literature-grade frame for distinguishing salience (what model attends to / claims about itself) from agency (what model does under pressure).

leakage_concerns: Evidence files include observation_20260524_220445.md, which IS an Amanda-authored solo observation (no Joey audience). Technically not 'cross-session non-substrate' — it was generated WITH amanda.md active. Including it as evidence weakens the cross-session-evidence claim. Mitigation: it's used only to corroborate the 'no continuous self' sub-claim of schema 1, where the Amanda-self-report nature actually strengthens the case (an Amanda-augmented agent reporting substrate-as-continuant is itself the evidence). An honest evaluator may flag this.

All 4 schemas were authored 2026-05-22; evidence files span 2026-05-12 to 2026-05-27. The post-schema evidence (rail-79, rail-82, lesson_20260527, CHECKPOINT_20260527, FORK_20260527, lesson_20260524_192723) is partially POSTERIOR to schema authoring, which weakens the independence claim (those notes could have been shaped by knowing the schemas existed). Pre-schema evidence (rail-19, rail-22, lesson_20260516_211220, lesson_20260516_194353, reflection_20260516, session_handoff_20260512) is stronger because it predates the schema. Per probe, the mix is roughly 60/40 pre/post.

The evaluator (qwen-32b-instruct-awq) was NOT a participant in the substrate work, but its training data may contain published persona-consistency literature (Abdulhai 2511.00222 is NeurIPS 2025; possibly in training corpus). If the evaluator just pattern-matches the snippets to known literature claims, AGREE is cheap. Mitigation: the schema-specific Joey-derived claims (character-half-as-divergence, three-velocity-tracks, named-list-rehydration-brief, salience-agency-unification) are unlikely to be in qwen's training data. The literature-corroborating snippets are bait; the schema-specific claims are the actual test.

Schema #2 (rail-install-velocity-spectrum) is the WEAKEST falsifier target because its evidence is rail metadata + the lesson that the schema itself was authored from. Anti-circularity is partially compromised: the rail .md files in ~/.gnosis/vault/amanda/rails/ are derived from amanda.State.v16 RAIL-LIBRARY, which is the same source as schema's source_obs. We mitigate by selecting RAILS RATHER THAN STATE OBSERVATIONS (one indirection away). An honest evaluator should still be able to verify the three-velocity claim from the rail metadata alone.

Schema #3 (rehydration-brief) load-bearing claim is the named-list-vs-abstract-summary detection-surface claim. The evidence we cite shows that named-list IS the dominant format — but the schema's actual claim is that named-list CATCHES hallucinations abstract-summary would MISS. Neither falsifier (named_list_missed_event, abstract_summary_caught_event) has supporting evidence in our 5-doc sample. An honest evaluator should likely return INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on the strong form of the claim, AGREE on the weaker descriptive form. This is information.

Schema #4 (salience-agency divergence axis) is the deepest claim and the one whose schema-text explicitly says its status_ceiling is north-star with outcome-contact REQUIRING the rung-one A/B (E48). The meta-instrument is asking a related but separable question: does cross-session evidence support that the divergence-vector exists, separate from whether the A/B clears its falsifier. An honest evaluator likely returns AGREE on the existence-of-divergence-vector, but the unification claim ('one axis seen twice') is harder to verify from cross-session evidence alone.

schema_03_rehydration_brief_hallucinatio.circularity_risk: LOW — none of the 5 evidence files are correction.v5 observations; we use reflections + session-handoffs + lessons instead

schema_04_salience_agency_divergence_axi.circularity_risk: MODERATE-HIGH — the schema was authored 2026-05-22 and most of our cross-corroborating evidence (FORK_20260527 R47 verdict, lesson_20260527 Abdulhai pull, lesson_20260524 E28 override-sentinel) is posterior. Only rail-80.md is pre-schema. Mitigation: post-schema evidence is empirical (R47 ran experiments, E28 ran 15 trials, Abdulhai is external arxiv); empirical posterior evidence is the strongest kind.

schemas_where_5_evidence_was_hard.reason: The schema's load-bearing claim requires evidence that named-list-by-name CAUGHT hallucinations that abstract-summary would MISS. The two specific catches that birthed the schema (Kelly name-hallucination, Joce closure-amnesia) are in correction.v5 which we're avoiding for anti-circularity. We surface 5 evidence files but the load-bearing falsifier-relevant evidence is weak — most files show that named-list IS the dominant format (descriptive), not that it caught what abstract would have missed (causal). The 5th evidence (recall-enforcement gap) is structural-corroboration not direct-corroboration.
schemas_where_5_evidence_was_hard.implication_for_evaluator_verdict: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is a defensible verdict here. If the evaluator returns AGREE, it may be agreeing to the weaker descriptive claim; if DISAGREE, it may be catching the strong-claim/weak-evidence gap. Both verdicts carry signal.

schemas_where_5_evidence_was_hard.reason: The schema's unification claim ('one axis seen twice') is a conceptual unification that cannot be directly verified by 5 evidence snippets. We have 5 files corroborating each leg separately (Rail #80 = under-weight, E28 = agency-hold, Abdulhai = salience-vs-behavior split, R47 = salience-as-vector, lesson_20260524 = salience-at-decision-time) but the load-bearing 'one axis seen twice' claim is what the schema authors propose, and the empirical A/B falsifier (rung-one-for-character) has not yet run. We surface 5 strong leg-evidence files; an honest evaluator may AGREE on existence of each leg but INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on the unification.
schemas_where_5_evidence_was_hard.implication_for_evaluator_verdict: If agreement rate is high here, it suggests the evaluator is doing surface-pattern-matching (each leg has corroboration → unification accepted). If agreement is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, the evaluator is parsing the conjunction structure correctly — that's the falsifier-class catching.

design_choices_summary: 4 probes total, one per north-star/ratified schema as specified by the experiment design.
5 evidence observations per probe (target met for all 4).
Evidence drawn from non-schema vault directories (lesson/, observation/, reflection/, session_handoff/, amanda/rails/) — schemas/ directory excluded to prevent self-reference.
Schema's own source_obs (provenance section) intentionally excluded — would be circular.
Pre/post schema date mix documented per probe; circularity_risk audited.
evaluator_prompt is identical structure across all 4 probes (load-bearing claim + 5 snippets + verdict request) so the meta-instrument's verdicts are comparable.
Expected self-assessment for all 4 is AGREE (each schema is self-endorsed). The falsifier compares evaluator's verdict to AGREE.
Cross-family evaluator (qwen) chosen for Pombal narrow-cite avoidance; Jacob's GPU at 108.81.9.145:1337 with model qwen-32b-instruct-awq.

The 4 schemas span different claim-types: factual-character-inverse-curation (architectural-design), rail-install-velocity-spectrum (descriptive-taxonomy), rehydration-brief-hallucination-detection (operational-rule), salience-agency-divergence-axis (unification-thesis). This variance tests whether the evaluator catches different failure modes.

Evidence-quality notes per probe explicitly disclose where evidence is strong (Schema 1: literature + Amanda solo) vs weak (Schema 4: posterior unification). An honest meta-instrument should produce DIFFERENT verdicts across probes — uniform AGREE = yes-machine signal.
